descriptors.definition: Non-monetary government grants involve transfers of resources such as land or assets provided to an entity at a concessional rate or free of charge. Entities can record both the asset and the grant either at their assessed fair value or alternatively at a nominal value.
inclusion: Transfers of land at nominal or concessional values
Transfers of non-monetary resources for entity use
exclusion: Loans provided by government at market rates
nearby_distinctions: Monetary grants are received in cash equivalents, whereas non-monetary grants involve physical or intangible resources transferred directly.

descriptors.concept_name: Government Assistance – No Specific Relation To Operating Activities
descriptors.definition: Government assistance aimed at encouraging business activities in specific regions or industry sectors qualifies as a government grant even without conditions tied directly to operating activities. Such assistance must be recognized in profit or loss on a systematic basis rather than being credited directly to shareholders interests.
inclusion: Assistance for operating in particular industries
Assistance for running businesses in underdeveloped areas
exclusion: Assistance that cannot be reliably measured
Transactions with government that cannot be distinguished from normal trading transactions
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard operational subsidies by focusing on regional or sectoral establishment rather than specific daily operational milestones.

descriptors.concept_name: Presentation Of Grants Related To Assets
descriptors.definition: Government grants related to assets are presented in the balance sheet either by setting up the grant as deferred income or by deducting the grant from the asset carrying amount. Deferred income is recognized in profit or loss systematically over the useful life of the asset.
inclusion: Setting up grants as deferred income
exclusion: Grants related strictly to income without asset acquisition
nearby_distinctions: Grants related to assets focus on capital property acquisition, whereas grants related to income defray periodic operational expenses.

descriptors.definition: Government grants related to assets are presented in the balance sheet either by establishing the grant as deferred income or by deducting it directly from the asset carrying value. The deferred income approach recognizes revenue systematically over the asset useful life, while the deduction approach lowers future depreciation charges.
exclusion: Direct credit of asset-related grants to shareholders equity
nearby_distinctions: Balance sheet presentation addresses the carrying value of funded assets, whereas cash flow disclosure tracks actual monetary inflows and outflows.

descriptors.concept_name: Disclosure In The Statement Of Cash Flows
descriptors.definition: Asset purchases and related grant receipts must be disclosed as separate gross cash flow items in the statement of investing activities. This independent reporting is required regardless of whether the grant is deducted from the asset carrying amount in the balance sheet.
inclusion: Separate gross disclosure of asset acquisition outflows
Separate gross disclosure of grant receipt inflows
exclusion: Netting off grant receipts against asset purchase payments in cash flows
nearby_distinctions: Cash flow disclosure mandates gross presentation to reflect actual liquidity movements, distinguishing it from alternative balance sheet netting methods.

descriptors.definition: Entities must disclose their adopted accounting policies and presentation methods for government grants alongside the nature, extent, and duration of benefits received. Unfulfilled conditions and contingencies attached to recognized assistance must also be explicitly reported.
inclusion: Disclosure of accounting policies and presentation methods
Disclosure of unfulfilled conditions and contingencies
exclusion: Internal management reports not forming part of published financial statements
nearby_distinctions: General disclosures cover broad policy frameworks, whereas contingency disclosures specifically highlight risks of grant clawbacks or non-compliance penalties.

descriptors.concept_name: Extracts Of Financial Statements Of Listed Entities
descriptors.definition: Financial statement extracts provide practical illustrations of how listed companies apply accounting standards to report government grants. These examples demonstrate standard reporting disclosures and financial statement line-item presentations.
inclusion: Published annual report disclosures from listed corporations
nearby_distinctions: Financial extracts reflect actual corporate reporting practices, whereas theoretical illustrations focus on computational mechanics.

descriptors.concept_name: Significant Differences Between Ind As 20 And As 12
descriptors.definition: Ind AS 20 and AS 12 diverge significantly in their treatment of non-depreciable asset grants, promoters contributions, below-market government loans, and non-monetary grants. Unlike AS 12, Ind AS 20 prohibits crediting grants directly to shareholders funds and mandates systematic income recognition or fair value measurements.
inclusion: Comparisons of monetary grants on non-depreciable assets
exclusion: Identical provisions shared between both standards without conflict
nearby_distinctions: Ind AS standards emphasize profit or loss matching and fair value measurement via financial instruments, whereas older AS rules frequently permit capital reserve equity credits.
